text: In a poll with a ±3-point margin of error, a candidate leading by 4 points is clearly ahead.

room.label: students (demo crowd)
room.note: No published poll has measured this belief yet. The 5C pilot survey replaces this split with real student answers.

truthSource.label: Pew Research Center: understanding the margin of error
truthSource.oneLine: The margin of error on the gap between two candidates is about twice the reported margin, so ±3 becomes roughly ±6 on a lead. It also covers only sampling error.

lesson.tip: A lead smaller than about twice the margin of error isn’t a clear lead. When a poll graphic says someone is “ahead,” compare the gap to double the margin.
